_comment: Everything about the department vocabulary lives here. It replaces the old departments.json.
The chain the site walks, and where each link is defined:
surgery ──► primary department ──► secondary department ──► speciality ──► hospital, doctor
SubDept_Map.tsv          this file, 'secondary'          Dept_Map.tsv       Inventory.xlsx
Two of the four links are sheets you own. This file holds the two judgement calls:
which spellings mean the same thing, and which department may stand in for another.
canonical spelling → the spellings the inventory actually contains.
Applied to EVERY speciality on the way in — hospitals, doctors, Dept_Map.tsv and the
Specialities column of SubDept_Map.tsv alike. That is the point: before this existed, a
value in SubDept_Map had to reproduce the sheet's typos exactly or it silently matched
nothing. Now either spelling works and the site displays the correct one.
Add a line here when a refresh reports a new spelling of something already known.
Do NOT add a line to merge two genuinely different specialities — that is what
Dept_Map.tsv is for.
One inventory cell that names two specialities. Split so each is matched on its own:
a hospital listed as 'Hair Transplant & Dermataology' really does do dermatology, and
before this it could only ever be found by a hair-transplant search.
'IVF & Gynec' is deliberately NOT split — it is the name of a single unit, and
Dept_Map.tsv already routes it to both Fertility and Gynaecology.
department → departments that may also satisfy it.
A secondary department says: this surgery is commonly performed by another team, so a
hospital listing that other department should also match. Resolution is transitive and
cycle-safe. Without these, 'Piles' returns nothing — its department is Proctology and no
active hospital lists Proctology, even though Proctology exists in the speciality master.
How a speciality the inventory contains but Dept_Map.tsv does not is handled.
Rules under 'apply' are deterministic and reversible — they restate a mapping you already
made, they never invent one. Anything they cannot settle is written to
incoming/Dept_Map.suggested.tsv with a confidence score and is NOT used: those hospitals
stay unreachable until you paste the line you agree with into Dept_Map.tsv. That is the
same bargain as `npm run check` — name the problem, do not paper over it.
_modifierWordsComment: Words that qualify a speciality without changing which department it belongs to.
'Surgical Gastroenterology' and 'Medical Gastroenterology' differ only by one of these,
so a new one of the pair inherits the department of the one already mapped.
The rule is set equality on the remaining words, NOT a shared word. A shared word is
not enough: 'Renal Transplant' and 'Hair Transplant' share 'transplant' and belong
nowhere near each other, and the loose version of this rule filed kidney transplants
under Aesthetic. If the remaining words are not identical it is a judgement call, and
judgement calls are suggested, never applied.
